maria.k: Quick question — who owns the smokehouse vs deepbench split + validation signals for new model onboard? I feel product should own acceptance criteria, but infra/bench should own runner and perf contracts. Thoughts?

ben.p: My take: acceptance thresholds (QA/golden) yes product. But the *operational contract* (APIs, timeouts, sample budgets) should live with eng-ml/bench. We keep ownerships clean: product says "what good looks like"; bench says "we'll run this and report pass/fail and perf numbers".

sasha: FWIW we've been tripping over this when teams ask for bespoke probe configs. Maybe we need a small shim API that maps product's "acceptance set" to bench probes + runtime knobs. That way product doesn't learn bench infra details.

maria.k: Agree. Proposal: 1) product owns golden input sets & outcome predicates (quality metrics), 2) eng-ml owns probe orchestration, runtime profiles, and cost budgets, 3) observability/telemetry contract owned by devx so SLO/alerting standard is consistent.

ben.p: +1. Also want to clarify where compatibility checks live: tokenizer/abi sanity should be fast local checks (on ingest), but full KV/cache/runtime smoke should be on the bench cluster. We should document the handoff surfaces.

sasha: Can we sketch minimal handshake? Something like:
```
ModelDescriptor -> {model_id, tokenizer_hash, expected_vocab_size}
PreflightRunner -> returns {abi_ok: bool, quick_sample: sample_outputs}
BenchOrchestrator -> accepts ModelDescriptor + acceptance_set_id + runtime_profile -> returns {pass/fail, perf_metrics, artifacts}
```
This keeps each component small.

maria.k: That looks good. Who implements the PreflightRunner shim? Is it eng-ml or intake pipeline?

ben.p: Intake should do the tokenization/abi checks as part of the ingest CI. PreflightRunner in eng-ml will be a lightweight wrapper to run a few short golden prompts inside the runtime variant we plan to serve (to catch runtime-only issues).

devx: Noting telemetry: bench should emit the canonical fields: model_id, run_id, sample_id, latency_p50/p95/p99, cost_estimate_tokens, pass_flags. We should version the schema (v1) and put it in the console docs.

maria.k: Let's also add a gating SLA: fast preflight must finish < 2m, bench smoke < 15m for the shallow suite, deeper bench (regression tests) can be async with notification.

ben.p: Tradeoff: if we enforce <15m we may need dedicated capacity or queued parallelism. For big models the shallow suite might still be heavy. Suggest we add a sample budget per model class (small/medium/large) and make the bench scheduler SLA-aware.

sasha: Action items:
- eng-ml: write a one-page handshake spec for ModelDescriptor/PreflightRunner/BenchOrchestrator (owner: ben.p)
- product: publish acceptance predicate templates + example golden sets (owner: maria.k)
- devx: define telemetry schema v1 and update console ingestion docs (owner: devx)
- intake: ensure tokenizer/abi quick checks are part of ingest CI (owner: sasha)

maria.k: Can we get owners to ack here? If yes I'll file a tiny RFC and link the spec.

ben.p: Ack — will draft handshake spec today.

sasha: Ack — will add ingest CI ticket.

devx: Ack — will start telemetry doc draft.

evaluator-bot: Automated note: "Added task cards to #onboard-triage for ben.p, maria.k, sasha, devx" :white_check_mark:

maria.k: Great, thanks. One more thought — we should include a fallback policy in the handshake: if bench smoke fails with perf issues, fallback can pin to earlier runtime quantization profile and re-run quick smoke. I'll add as a section in the RFC.

ben.p: Good call. I'll include a sample pseudocode for automatic retry/fallback logic in the spec.

sasha: Perfect. Closing this thread — will follow up in the RFC PR.
